q: What is a baby cat called?
x: Kittens are born blind and deaf, and open their eyes after about one to two weeks.

q: What is a baby dog called?
x: Puppies sleep up to 18 to 20 hours a day while they grow.

q: What is a baby kangaroo called?
x: A newborn joey is about the size of a jellybean and crawls into its mother's pouch.

q: Which animal is known as the king of the jungle?
x: Despite the nickname, lions mostly live in grasslands and savannas, not jungles.

q: Which bird is famous for being unable to fly and living in Antarctica?
x: Penguins use their wings as flippers to swim fast underwater.

q: What do pandas mainly eat?
x: A giant panda can eat 26 to 84 pounds of bamboo every day.

q: Which animal has a long trunk?
x: An elephant's trunk has tens of thousands of muscle units and can lift heavy logs or pick up a single peanut.

q: Which animal is the tallest in the world?
x: A giraffe has the same number of neck bones as a human: seven.

q: What do you call a baby frog?
x: Tadpoles breathe with gills and later develop lungs and legs as they become frogs.

q: What is a baby cow called?
x: A calf can usually stand within an hour of being born.

q: What is a baby horse called?
x: Foals can stand and walk within a few hours of birth.

q: What is a baby sheep called?
x: Lambs can recognize their mother's call within a few days of birth.

q: What is a baby pig called?
x: Piglets are born with sharp teeth, which breeders often notice at birth.

q: What is a baby goat called?
x: Goat kids can walk within minutes of being born.

q: What is a baby bear called?
x: Bear cubs are born tiny, often weighing less than a pound, while their mothers hibernate.

q: Which sea creature has eight arms?
x: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood.

q: What type of animal is a dolphin?
x: Dolphins breathe air through a blowhole and nurse their young with milk.

q: What type of animal is a penguin?
x: Penguins are birds with dense, waterproof feathers, even though they cannot fly.

q: Which animal lays the biggest egg of any living bird?
x: An ostrich egg weighs about three pounds, roughly the same as two dozen chicken eggs.

q: What do caterpillars turn into?
x: Inside the chrysalis or cocoon, the caterpillar's body is almost completely reorganized.

q: Which animal produces honey?
x: A honeybee makes only about a twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in its whole lifetime.

q: Which large cat has black stripes on orange fur?
x: Every tiger's stripe pattern is unique, like a human fingerprint.

q: Which animal is known for carrying its home on its back?
x: A snail's shell grows with it and is made of calcium carbonate.

q: Which animal is the fastest on land over short distances?
x: A cheetah can reach about 60 to 70 miles per hour in short bursts.

q: What is the name for a female chicken?
x: A hen can lay about 250 to 300 eggs a year in good conditions.

q: What is a male deer called?
x: Bucks grow and shed a new set of antlers each year.

q: Which animal has black and white stripes?
x: No two zebras have exactly the same stripe pattern.

q: Which animal is known for changing color to blend in with surroundings?
x: Chameleons also change color to communicate mood and regulate temperature.

q: Which animal sleeps hanging upside down in caves?
x: Bats can lock their feet in a gripping position so they hang without using muscle effort.

q: What do cows eat?
x: Cows are ruminants with a four-part stomach that helps them digest plants.

q: Which bird is known for its colorful tail feathers fanned in display?
x: Only the male peafowl, the peacock, has the dramatic train of feathers.

q: Which bird is known for hooting at night?
x: Owls can rotate their heads about 270 degrees.

q: Which animal is known as man's best friend?
x: Dogs were domesticated from wolves at least 15,000 years ago.

q: What is a group of lions called?
x: A pride is often made up of related females, their cubs, and a few adult males.

q: What is a group of wolves called?
x: A wolf pack is usually a family: a breeding pair and their offspring.

q: What is a group of fish called?
x: Swimming in schools helps fish avoid predators and find food.

q: What is a group of cows usually called?
x: Cattle in a herd form social bonds and have preferred companions.

q: What is a group of birds flying together often called?
x: Flying in a flock can save energy and gives more eyes to watch for danger.

q: Which sea animal has a hard shell, claws, and walks sideways?
x: Crabs walk sideways because of how their legs' joints bend.

q: Which animal is known for its black-and-white fur and for living in bamboo forests of China?
x: Giant pandas live in a few mountain ranges in central China.

q: Which animal is the largest living species of bear that lives in the Arctic?
x: A polar bear's skin is black under its translucent, hollow-looking fur.

q: Which sea mammal is known for its tusks and lives in the Arctic?
x: Walrus tusks are elongated canine teeth and can grow over three feet long.

q: Which animal is a monotreme that lays eggs and has a duck-like bill?
x: Male platypuses have venomous spurs on their hind legs.

q: Which animal hops and carries its young in a pouch?
x: A kangaroo cannot walk backward easily, which is one reason it appears on Australia's coat of arms.

q: Which animal eats mainly eucalyptus leaves?
x: Koalas sleep around 18 to 22 hours a day because eucalyptus gives little energy.

q: Which insect is known for building hills and living in a colony with a queen?
x: Some ant colonies have millions of individuals working together.

q: Which insect glows in the dark on summer nights?
x: Fireflies are actually beetles that make light through a chemical reaction.

q: Which animal is the national bird symbol of the United States?
x: The bald eagle's head is not actually bald; the name comes from an older meaning of 'white-headed'.

q: Which reptile has a hard shell and can pull its head inside?
x: A turtle's shell is part of its skeleton, fused to its ribs and spine.

q: Which reptile has no legs and moves by slithering?
x: Snakes smell by flicking their forked tongues to collect scent particles.

q: What sound does a cow make?
x: Cows have regional 'accents' in their moos, according to some farm studies.

q: Which animal gives us wool?
x: Sheep have been raised for wool for at least 8,000 years.

q: What color are flamingos, mostly?
x: Flamingos get their pink color from pigments in the algae and shrimp they eat.

q: Which animal is known for its very long neck and spotted coat in the African savanna?
x: A giraffe's tongue can be up to about 20 inches long.

q: Which sea creature has a star-shaped body?
x: Starfish, properly called sea stars, can regrow lost arms.

q: Which sea creature has stinging tentacles and a bell-shaped body with no brain?
x: Jellyfish are about 95 percent water and have existed for hundreds of millions of years.

q: Which large shark is famous for a dorsal fin that appears in the movie Jaws?
x: Great whites can detect tiny electrical fields from prey using special pores.

q: Which fish is known for its striped orange body and living in anemones, like Nemo?
x: Clownfish have a mucus coating that protects them from the anemone's stings.

q: Which insect makes silk to build a cocoon and is raised for fabric?
x: A single silkworm cocoon can be unwound into a thread nearly a mile long.

q: Which animal spends its life in trees, moves very slowly, and hangs upside down?
x: Algae sometimes grow in a sloth's fur, giving it a greenish tint.

q: Which primate is the closest living relative of humans, along with the bonobo?
x: Humans and chimpanzees share about 98 to 99 percent of their DNA.

q: What is a male lion known for having?
x: A darker, fuller mane often signals a healthier, stronger male.

q: What is a female pig called?
x: A sow can have two litters a year, each with ten or more piglets.

q: What is a female sheep called?
x: Ewes usually give birth to one or two lambs in spring.

q: What is a female horse called?
x: A mare carries her foal for about 11 months.

q: Which animal is the national symbol of Australia, seen on its coat of arms with the emu?
x: Both animals were chosen because neither can easily move backward.

q: Which animal says 'quack'?
x: Ducks have waterproof feathers thanks to oil from a gland near the tail.

q: Which animal makes webs to catch its food?
x: Spider silk is stronger than steel of the same thickness.

q: What do herbivores eat?
x: Cows, rabbits, and elephants are all herbivores.

q: What do we call animals that eat only meat?
x: Cats and hawks are examples of animals built for a meat-based diet.

q: What do we call animals that eat both plants and meat?
x: Bears, pigs, and humans are omnivores.

q: What is the process called when some animals sleep through winter?
x: During hibernation, an animal's heart rate and body temperature drop dramatically.

q: What is it called when birds travel long distances each year to warmer places?
x: Arctic terns migrate from the Arctic to Antarctica and back each year.

q: Which animal is a pet that purrs and chases mice?
x: Cats purr at a frequency of roughly 25 to 150 hertz.

q: Which huge dinosaur had a long neck and ate plants, like Brachiosaurus?
x: Sauropods were the largest land animals ever to walk the Earth.

q: Which dinosaur is famous for its giant head and tiny arms and is often called the 'tyrant lizard king'?
x: T. rex had a bite force among the strongest of any land animal ever.

q: Which dinosaur had three horns on its face and a large bony frill?
x: Its name means 'three-horned face'.

q: Which dinosaur had bony plates along its back and spikes on its tail?
x: Stegosaurus had a brain about the size of a lime.

q: Which extinct hairy relative of the elephant lived during the Ice Age?
x: Woolly mammoths lived alongside early humans and survived on Wrangel Island until about 4,000 years ago.

q: What do we call scientists who study fossils of ancient life?
x: Paleontologists learn about dinosaurs from fossilized bones, eggs, and footprints.

q: Which animal's milk is used to make most of the cheese and butter in stores?
x: A dairy cow can produce more than 6 gallons of milk a day.

q: Which animal is the largest member of the cat family?
x: Siberian tigers can weigh over 600 pounds.

q: Which animal gives a black ink-like cloud to escape predators?
x: The ink also dulls a predator's sense of smell.

q: Which animal builds dams out of sticks and logs?
x: Beaver teeth never stop growing, and orange enamel makes them extra hard.

q: Which animal can regrow its tail if it is lost?
x: Many lizards detach their tail on purpose to escape a predator.

q: Which sea animal is a mammal and sings long songs underwater, with a hump on its back?
x: Male humpbacks sing complex songs that can last for 10 to 20 minutes.

q: What is the main food of a hummingbird?
x: Hummingbirds can flap their wings dozens of times per second and even hover.

q: Which animal is covered in sharp quills for protection?
x: A porcupine can have around 30,000 quills.

q: Which animal is known for storing fat in one or two humps in the desert?
x: A camel can drink over 30 gallons of water in about 15 minutes.

q: What is a female deer called?
x: Does usually give birth to one or two spotted fawns in late spring.

q: What is a male chicken called?
x: Roosters are known for crowing at dawn, but they can crow at other times too.

q: Which animal is the largest living land animal?
x: A big male African elephant can weigh about 6 tons.

q: In the fable, which animal beats the hare in a race?
x: The tale of the tortoise and the hare is attributed to Aesop.

q: What is a baby duck called?
x: Ducklings can swim within hours of hatching.

q: What is a baby hen or rooster called when it first hatches?
x: A chick starts peeping inside the egg a day or so before hatching.

q: What color is a polar bear's fur?
x: Each hair is actually clear and hollow; it only looks white because it scatters light.

q: What gas do fish take from the water through their gills?
x: Gills pull dissolved oxygen out of water as it flows over thin, blood-rich filaments.

q: Which flightless bird lives in Antarctica?
x: Penguins use their wings as flippers for swimming in the icy sea.

q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
x: Two hearts pump blood through the gills and one pumps it around the body.

q: Which sea animal has eight arms and can squirt ink?
x: An octopus squirts a cloud of ink to confuse predators while it escapes.
